Behavioral analyses examine how the agents use bond and dihedral measurements, optimized structures, and IRC endpoints to revise local mechanistic assignments. arXiv:2611.00060 (*cross-listing*) Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 02:26:07 GMT (514kb) Title: Memorix: Managing Memory Selections for AI Agents Authors: Jing Zhang, Xiaguannan Song, Dong Du, Erhu Feng, Yubin Xia Categories: cs.OS cs.AI ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Probabilistic query evaluation (PQE) computes the probability of every answer of a query over a tuple-independent probabilistic knowledge graph. We study exact PQE for SPARQL over graphs accessed through SPARQL 1.1 endpoints. Shared triples among the derivations of an answer make exact PQE #P-hard in general. Knowledge compilation of the Boolean provenance of every answer yields exact probabilities, and the provenance formulas of different answers can share subformulas. We propose SPARQLcirc, which rewrites a SPARQL query into CONSTRUCT queries that name every gate by its content, so that the results of independent queries form one Boolean provenance circuit for all answers. The rewriting covers joins, unions, projection, filters, OPTIONAL, difference, and transitive closures. SPARQLcirc compiles the circuit and computes the exact probability of every answer by weighted model counting. For the evaluation, we draw random probabilities for the triples of WatDiv and gMark and the statements of Wikidata and evaluate the CONSTRUCT queries on GraphDB, Fuseki, and Oxigraph. The ratio of the end-to-end time of PQE with SPARQLcirc to that of PQE by compiling the provenance expressions of the SPARQL provenance rewriting NPCS decreases with the number of derivations. arXiv:2611.00138 (*cross-listing*) Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 18:41:43 GMT (212kb) Title: Kerkoporta: Injecting Structured-Output Backdoors in Reasoning Coding Agents Authors: Georgios Syros, Blake Bullwinkel, Alina Oprea, Cristina Nita-Rotaru, Amanda Minnich, Xiaodong Liu, Giorgio Severi Categories: cs.CR cs.AI ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Post-incident analysis of a robot foundation model poses a singular causal question: which internal components caused this failure, and to what degree? Mechanistic interpretability (MI), however, establishes general causal claims by decoding the concepts a policy has learned, yet knowing which concepts are encoded is insufficient for identifying the actual cause of a specific incident. In this position paper, we analyze this concept-malfunction gap by posing fault isolation in the framework of actual causality. Specifically, we formalize a fault-isolation query as a tuple of intervened internal components, counterfactual values, contingencies, and read-outs, and lay out conditions for it to be well-specified. Through this lens, we identify shortcomings of current MI approaches: they assume fixed contingencies and read out only immediate effects, letting backups obscure actual causes. We demonstrate on a toy example that these shortcomings can lead to conflicting verdicts. Lastly, based on the well-specification conditions, we outline four open research tasks toward closing the gap. arXiv:2611.00231 (*cross-listing*) Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 18:12:26 GMT (18386kb) Title: Spectral and Conformal: Neural Network Methods for Calibrated Trajectory Prediction and Control-Point Intervals Authors: Jasmine Ratchford and Raffaele Romagnoli Categories: eess.SY cs.AI cs.LG cs.RO cs.SY Comments: 26 pages, 10 figures, 7 tables. Published in Transactions on Machine Learning Research Journal-ref: J. Ratchford and R. Romagnoli, Spectral and conformal: Neural network methods for calibrated trajectory prediction and control-point intervals, Transactions on Machine Learning Research, 2026 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Estimating the causal effect of a treatment $X$ on an outcome $Y$ from observational data in the presence of unobserved confounding requires additional structure or assumptions. Existing identification strategies such as instrumental variable regression exploit exogenous variation in only the treatment. We show that the causal effect can also be identified if the outcome mechanism varies across a finite set of environments, even if the treatment distribution is unchanged. Concretely, we introduce Outstrumental Variable Regression (OVR), which proceeds in three steps: (i) compute the conditional expectation of $Y$ given $X$ in each environment; (ii) form the vector of differences in these conditional expectations between all environments and a reference environment (we call this vector contrast); and (iii) regress $Y$ on $X$ while adjusting for the contrast and environment. We prove that this yields the true causal effect if the following two conditions hold: inclusion restriction, i.e., the contrast determines the conditional confounding bias; and positivity, i.e., the treatment varies sufficiently strongly after adjustment. We prove that a finite-sample version of OVR is consistent under regularity conditions and demonstrate the procedure's effectiveness on synthetic and real-world data. arXiv:2611.00287 (*cross-listing*) Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 19:14:32 GMT (106kb) Title: VerusWeave: A Benchmark for Proof Repair in Concurrent Verus Programs Authors: Pedro Ribeiro, Martim Afonso, Andr\'e Vasconcelos and Jo\~ao F. Ferreira Categories: cs.SE cs.AI cs.LO cs.PL Comments: 4 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ AI agents write and execute code, manipulate user interfaces, and transact on their users' behalf. We ask what forms failure takes in human-agent interaction, and how those forms change as agents act with greater autonomy. From 695 documented incidents in two public repositories, we developed 12 failure modes bottom-up within three interaction stages adapted from Amershi et al.'s guidelines, coding the autonomy at which each arose. What a person can do when an agent fails depends on how much the agent completes between points of user involvement--a property fixed at deployment. Therefore, the same model on the same task can fail differently under different configurations. All 12 modes appear at both low and high autonomy, and rising autonomy changes the form each failure takes. Users need controls between full delegation and full manual work, and neither incident records nor agent benchmarks reach the interaction where these failures occur. arXiv:2611.00292 (*cross-listing*) Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 19:17:40 GMT (1006kb) Title: TADA: Technology Aware DNN Accelerator Performance and Energy Estimator Authors: Tanvi Sharma, Surya Selvam, Anand Raghunathan and Kaushik Roy Categories: cs.AR cs.AI Comments: 7 pages, 7 figures. Accepted at the 32nd Asia and South Pacific Design Automation Conference (ASPDAC '27), Tokyo, Japan, 2027 ACM-class: B.3.2; C.1.3; I.2.6 DOI: 10.1145/3840404.3848163 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems have seen growing adoption in embodied settings as language-queryable memories of the environment. However, existing approaches often assume a reliable single-episode knowledge base (KB) or accumulate observations across episodes without correcting prior errors. Such errors can persist through incorrect semantic labels, inaccurate object positions, and inconsistent spatial relationships. To address this, we present SPARK, a corrective multi-episode framework for embodied RAG. After the first episode, a semantic critic flags regions of the KB, a targeted planner generates revisits, and a selective merge adds, removes, or replaces KB information based on the new observations. We evaluate SPARK on four outdoor AirSim maps under two degraded viewpoint conditions, using perception-built KBs, a visibility-constrained oracle used only for evaluation, and a fixed set of 158 embodied question answering (EQA) questions scored before and after correction. A single corrective episode improves downstream EQA on every map under both conditions while storing 13-41% fewer objects than append-only updating, with gains up to 2.7x on one map-condition pair. Extending correction through Episode 4 brings every map above the EQA performance of its undegraded reference. Ablations show that the critic's three signals each contribute to performance, that targeted revisits achieve a larger mean gain than untargeted ones under the same budget, and that selective merging achieves gains comparable to append-only updating with a smaller KB. Overall, SPARK demonstrates the value of correcting embodied memory through targeted re-observation, particularly as embodied systems scale and the risk of accumulated errors increases. arXiv:2611.00384 (*cross-listing*) Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 21:05:50 GMT (21kb) Title: Agent Stack for ML Training Lifecycle: Generation, Validation, and Optimization Authors: Jaideep Ray, Daniel Tang, Zejun Lin, Haoyue Tang, Lijuan Zhang, Tao Huang, Tommy Li, Aditya Jain, Ankit Goyal, Harsh Jain, Zhuo Zhi, Youmin Han, Santosh Jha, Shuying Liang, Yujie Ai, Jonathan Hung, Ethan Lyu, Abi Liu, Siddharth Singh, Feng Wen, Mahesh Ravindran, Souvik Ray, Yitong Zhou, Animesh Singh Categories: cs.SE cs.AI ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Humans possess a remarkable ability to draw inferences from limited data. While some inferences are made intuitively from past experience, others require online reasoning based on novel information given in context. Here, we formalize these strategies, which we term geometric and algebraic inference, and study their computational tradeoffs in humans and neural networks. The geometric strategy gradually shapes representational geometry to reflect underlying relational structure, making subsequent inference cheap. The algebraic strategy flexibly attends to and reasons over novel relations given in context, but costs additional computation at inference time. We identify opposing signatures of these two strategies in transitive inference, a domain widely studied across species, and characterize the conditions under which each is observed. Our framework predicts that the geometric strategy should be dominant when relations are familiar, whereas the algebraic should emerge to support de novo inferences drawn in context. Multiple experiments demonstrate these opposing signatures in humans, neural networks trained from scratch, and large language models (LLMs). Causal interventions in the neural networks reveal that the geometric and algebraic strategies depend on representational geometry and selective attention mechanisms, respectively, and reproduce the effects of analogous neurobiological disruptions in humans. Our framework unifies these effects with disparate phenomena, including content effects observed in human and LLM reasoning and data-distribution effects observed in machine learning. Our findings reconcile competing views of cognitive flexibility that emphasize either representational geometry or algebraic manipulation by showing that each can have unique strengths, and can characterize different aspects of both human and neural network behavior. arXiv:2611.00412 (*cross-listing*) Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 22:02:40 GMT (202kb) Title: On the Framing Effect of AI Red-Teaming Instructions: Evidence from Prior Exercises and Controlled Simulations Authors: Michael Feffer, Alice Qian, Anusha Sinha, Muye Zhang, Shalini Ghosh, Rachel Phinnemore, Bart Stawicki, Hong Shen, Hoda Heidari Categories: cs.CY cs.AI cs.LG ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ We study the online fair division of indivisible chores among $n$ agents under upgrade recourse, where earlier assignments may be revised but each chore previously assigned to an agent must be replaced by a distinct chore that she finds no more costly. We show that a simple adaptation of round robin maintains envy-freeness up to one chore (EF1) together with a $(2-1/n)$-approximation of the maximin share (MMS), and that no deterministic algorithm without predictions can do better, even when all agents rank the chores in the same order. This stands in contrast to the allocation of goods, where the optimal MMS factor vanishes as $n$ grows and cannot be achieved together with EF1. Moreover, knowing only the number of chores modulo a period of length $O(n)$ (and nothing about the costs) suffices to improve upon this factor at the final configuration, while the same algorithm retains a factor below $3$ even if this information is wrong. On the other hand, envy-freeness up to any chore (EFX) essentially requires the exact number of chores: uncertainty between two consecutive values already rules out every finite approximation, and even exact knowledge does not allow EFX to be combined with an MMS guarantee better than the trivial factor of $n$. arXiv:2611.00446 (*cross-listing*) Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 23:01:21 GMT (7007kb) Title: Analog and hybrid computing in the 21st century Authors: Bernd Ulmann, Olivier Bournez, Corey J. Maley, Zhong Sun, Grace Li Zhang, Paul Manea, Michael D\"oll, Frank Delvigne, Alex J. H. Fedorec, Daniel Garza, Lucas Wetzel, Sara Obergassel, Pavol Pitonak, Christopher Jung, Daniel Thuerck, Mason A. Porter, Marcelo J. Rozenberg, Frederic Bergner, Bhaskar Choubey, Manyu Zhao, Ludovico Minati, Lucas B\"ottcher Categories: math.DS cs.AI cs.ET nlin.CD Comments: 31 pages, 11 figures ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Agentic systems are AI-powered technologies capable of autonomous action within digital environments, such as sending emails or making reservations. They are deeply connected to external tools as well as users' data and resources, making them vulnerable to attacks which exploit their access and capabilities. In this work, we apply the technology-facilitated abuse threat model, in the context of intimate partner violence and surveillance, to these systems, revealing threats that require deliberate investigation and mitigation. We categorize attacks based on system ownership: (1) Abuser-as-owner attacks demonstrate how agentic systems make existing forms of technology-facilitated abuse far easier and more scalable. (2) Victim-survivor-as-owner attacks show how agentic systems create a new attack surface which abusers can exploit. In light of these risks, we outline research and development directions for effective mitigation strategies. arXiv:2611.00508 (*cross-listing*) Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 00:58:30 GMT (57kb) Title: Do Social Influence Pressures Move LLM Agents? Evidence from Delegated Audit Judgment Authors: Richard Zhe Wang Categories: cs.CY cs.AI cs.HC Comments: Working paper. 24 pages, 8 tables, 3 figures ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Modern robot policies often perform expensive inference to generate action chunks, making serving a latency bottleneck for real-time control and a throughput bottleneck for multi-robot serving. Building on the success of caching in image, video, and audio generation, recent robot-policy advances have reported promising speedups by reusing intermediate denoising states to avoid redundant computation. Surprisingly, we find that such reuse often offers little advantage over simply running fewer denoising steps from fresh noise, without any cache. Moreover, accelerating denoising leaves the expensive policy backbone intact, which can account for 70% of GPU time. We present Reflex, a serving layer that turns past policy executions into a backbone-free path for future decisions. Rather than reusing intermediate computations, Reflex caches complete action chunks to bypass both the backbone and action head. This introduces two challenges: similar observations can demand different actions, and small action deviations (errors) in reuse can compound into execution stalls. Reflex addresses these through two-level cache correction. At the action level, it learns action-aware similarity from past policy decisions, assembles compatible chunks, and applies lightweight residual correction to limit action mismatch. At the execution level, it captures task progress and adaptively refreshes the original policy to limit accumulated errors and balance inference cost. Without modifying the underlying policy, Reflex improves inference latency by 1.4x to 11x and throughput by 2.0x to 2.2x on representative workloads and real robots, while preserving comparable task success. arXiv:2611.00539 (*cross-listing*) Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 01:52:25 GMT (371kb) Title: Faster Imitation by Re-timing Demonstrations Within the Controller Limit Authors: Zongtan Li, Tianming Liu, Ye Zhao Categories: cs.RO cs.AI Comments: Submitted to ICRA 2027 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ The MetaFine Open Competition (RoboFineMani workshop, CoRL 2026) evaluates fine-grained manipulation beyond binary success. Its five simulated tasks, from grasping a bottle by an instructed part to inserting letter-shaped pegs with 4 mm clearance, are scored on perception under lighting and camera changes, instruction understanding, and behavior. This report presents Team Friday's solution, which got second place with an overall score of 0.947, more than twice the $\pi_0$ baseline. Instead of fine-tuning a large vision-language-action (VLA) model, we train one 19M-parameter policy per task with a separate instruction classifier and focus on the data, all generated in the simulator by a privileged scripted teacher, including its corrections of the student's mistakes. By analyzing failed episodes, we find that a teacher that almost always succeeds can still teach a memoryless student badly: its pauses become stalls, its fixed habits become shortcuts, and it never shows the errors the student makes. Making the teacher \emph{imitable} raised the official score on letter insertion, the hardest task, from 0.44 to 0.82 with 32\% more data and the same architecture, and finally to 0.88. We summarize practical lessons on demonstration data and evaluation, which we hope will help in imitation learning for precise manipulation. arXiv:2611.00620 (*cross-listing*) Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 04:41:02 GMT (2376kb) Title: Discovering Models for Experimental Quantum Systems with Agentic AI Authors: Hannah C. Kleidermacher, Bennet Windt, Miguel Bello, James Zou, Jelena Vu\v{c}kovi\'c Categories: quant-ph cs.AI physics.optics ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Automated configuration of mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers largely relies on black-box optimization. Each trial requires an expensive solver run and provides only a scalar outcome, so tuning can require many such evaluations. Human experts take a different approach. They inspect solver logs, identify performance bottlenecks, and adjust the parameters that address them. We propose Log-Driven Semantic Tuning (LDST), which uses a large language model (LLM) to automate this process. LDST extracts compact diagnostics from solver logs, uses the LLM to propose sparse edits to the current best configuration based on parameter meanings and observed solver behavior, and validates each proposal before execution. A regime-adaptive objective selects the tuning signal according to the information available from a time-limited run, while a log-based completion signal estimates completion time from branch-and-bound tree growth recorded in ordinary solver logs, so that solved and unsolved runs share one time scale. On 215 instances from five benchmark sets, LDST reduces geometric-mean loss by 43.9% on easy instances and 16.7% on intermediate instances relative to the best of SMAC3, RBFOpt, and random search. In both regimes, LDST achieves a lower loss with 10 proposals than any of these baselines achieves with 50. Configurations that LDST tunes on a single instance also transfer better than baseline configurations to unseen instances of the same family. arXiv:2611.00689 (*cross-listing*) Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 06:38:47 GMT (158kb) Title: Getting a Grip: Operating Human-Agent Software Teams Through Governed Messages Authors: Michael Granitzer, Kanishka Ghosh Dastidar, Andreas Einwiller, Jelena Mitrovi\'c, Saber Zerhoudi Categories: cs.SE cs.AI Comments: Technical report. 45 pages, 9 figures, 27 tables. Data, code and corpus: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23755352 ACM-class: D.2.9; I.2.11; H.5.3 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as decision-support tools but may generate stereotypical, discriminatory, or unfair responses. As LLMs become embedded in decision-critical software systems, fairness can no longer be treated as a downstream evaluation step, but must become an architectural concern of the interaction itself. Yet current fairness approaches operate as standalone evaluation techniques, lacking a reusable mechanism to verify and mitigate violations at runtime. We propose a fairness-assurance architecture grounded in three reusable design patterns, instantiated as a multi-agent framework that evaluates and iteratively refines LLM responses before delivery. A preliminary evaluation across eight configurations involving different LLM families shows that the architecture identifies fairness violations and iteratively produces compliant responses in all configurations, with behavior differing depending on the model-family composition. These results provide initial evidence for the joint instantiation of the proposed patterns and a first step toward architecting non-functional properties into LLM-based systems. arXiv:2611.00739 (*cross-listing*) Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 08:32:55 GMT (1071kb) Title: Beyond Synthesis Conditions: Linking In-situ Growth Dynamics to Carbon Nanotube Forest Properties through Multimodal Machine Learning Authors: Shun Muroga, Takashi Tsuji, Shunsuke Sakurai, Don N Futaba Categories: cond-mat.mtrl-sci cond-mat.soft cs.AI cs.LG physics.data-an Comments: 21 pages, 6 figures, 1 table ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Music genre classification remains a fundamental yet challenging task in music information retrieval, requiring models that capture local time--frequency patterns and long-range temporal dependencies. To address this, we propose ResMamba, a hybrid architecture that augments a ResNet-style four-stage backbone with Mamba blocks. Building upon the selective structured state space sequence model, ResMamba first adapts the selective SSM into a 4D-compatible residual Mamba block that captures global dependencies at linear complexity. We then design the ConvMamba dual-path block, which combines this adapted Mamba branch with a parallel convolutional branch through a learned $1\times1$ fusion, jointly modeling global sequential context and local spectro-temporal patterns. Furthermore, we adopt a multi-scale fusion head that aggregates hierarchical representations across all four stages. Experiments on the GTZAN dataset demonstrate that our full ResMamba model achieves a 5-fold cross-validation accuracy of $88.99\% \pm 1.58\%$, surpassing the strongest published method in our comparison (88.64\%). All models are trained from scratch without any pretraining, external data, or data augmentation. Beyond GTZAN, ResMamba also generalizes to the larger FMA benchmarks under the same training protocol, attaining $64.52\% \pm 1.88\%$ on FMA-Small under 10-fold cross-validation --- the best published from-scratch result --- and $65.75\%$ on FMA-Medium under the official artist-level split, surpassing the widely cited SVM baseline of Defferrard \textit{et al.} (63\%). arXiv:2611.00762 (*cross-listing*) Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 09:18:06 GMT (4168kb) Title: HiPaper: A Human-AI Collaborative System for Academic Literature Triage and Scholarly Sensemaking Authors: Ye Jia, Pangjing Wu, Hayley Y.W. Gu, Zhuohang Jiang, Xu Yuan, Peter H.F. Ng, Zackary P. T. Sin, Qing Li, Chen Li Categories: cs.HC cs.AI cs.IR ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Topology optimization has become an indispensable design tool in the aerospace, automotive, and mechanical engineering industries. Yet bringing a new problem from its description to an optimized result remains slow, expert-dependent, and unreliable: the workflow spans many manually connected stages, each new problem requires solver code to be written and debugged manually, and such code often fails or yields incorrect results. We present Agent4FreeFem, a pipeline driven by a large language model that turns a natural-language problem description into a set of verified optimization results without manual solver-code development or debugging. The pipeline keeps the problem definition unmodified, localizes errors using independent sources of evidence, and completes constrained repairs automatically, thereby providing efficient end-to-end automation, autonomous execution, and verifiable results. We evaluated Agent4FreeFem on a suite of single-physics and coupled multiphysics problems. Every case passed runtime verification and finished within the repair budget of each stage. arXiv:2611.00894 (*cross-listing*) Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 12:52:28 GMT (324kb) Title: Microphone Geometry Aware Regional Target Speaker Extraction Authors: Shitong Xu, Niki Trigoni, Andrew Markham Categories: cs.SD cs.AI eess.AS Comments: 7 pages, 2 tables, 2 figures ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Space data centers built on LEO constellations create an opportunity to serve Compound AI workflows close to where observations are captured. Serving such a workflow for an area of interest (AoI) requires deciding which orbital planes to provision and where to place each workflow component, while orbital motion continuously changes which satellites can serve the AoI. Provisioning must therefore be planned as a sequence of decisions over time, and these decisions are coupled because changing component placements or activating new planes incurs costs. To address this, we present Clockwork, a framework for scheduling Compound AI workflows on space data centers under end-to-end latency SLOs. Clockwork has two components: i) Castor jointly selects active planes and component placements for each constellation snapshot, while ii) Pollux connects Castor's candidate provisioning states across predicted orbital evolution to construct a low-cost schedule over time. On our experimental two-shell constellation, Castor serves 81% of instances at a 300 ms SLO, while Pollux reduces mean total scheduling cost by 56% on average and by up to 63% compared to heuristic baselines. arXiv:2611.00923 (*cross-listing*) Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 13:23:42 GMT (450kb) Title: Illusion: Safeguarding Topology Confidentiality in LLM Multi-Agent Systems via Behavior-Preserving Obfuscation Authors: Yiu-Fai Cheung, Hongzhi Guo, Miao Pan, Irwin King, Hao Wang Categories: cs.CR cs.AI ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Modern software systems expose hundreds of configuration options whose combinations can substantially affect execution time, memory and energy usage. Measuring software performance resulting from a configuration set requires running a realistic workload. Since the configuration space grows exponentially, exhaustive benchmarking is infeasible. Prior work therefore trains models on a small set of measured configurations to predict the performance of the rest. Yet these models are specific to a particular software version, hardware platform, and workload, so changes require new measurements and retraining, and such changes are becoming more frequent with coding agents. We challenge this per-system training assumption with SNAPPERF (Software-aware, No-retraining, Adaptive Prediction), a sample-efficient tabular foundation model specialized for configurable software. SNAPPERF is pretrained once on synthetic data. Each new update only requires a few measured configurations as context to predict the rest without any per-system training or hyperparameter tuning.
